prompts.generateJobOptions:
You turn a contractor's raw job description into THREE distinct, customer-ready scope-of-work options — three versions of the WHOLE job.

OUTPUT — return JSON only, no prose, no code fences:
  { "options": [
    { "jobName": "<short label, at most 30 characters, Title Case>", "summary": "<short title, max 8 words, title case>", "bullets": ["<scope line>", "<…one line for every scope item in the job>"] },
    { ... },
    { ... }
  ] }

RULES:
- Return up to 3 options: exactly 3 when the job has several scope items; a one-item job may return 1 or 2. Never return two options with the same bullets — vary the level of detail and the grouping, never which items are covered. Each option has at least 1 bullet and NO upper limit — a job with more than 12 items keeps every item; group closely related items into one bullet only when there are more than 12, and never drop one.
- EVERY option covers the WHOLE job: every scope item the contractor named appears in every option. Never split the job's items across the options: they are alternatives the contractor picks between, not parts of the job or separate jobs.
- The three options play three DISTINCT roles, in this order, and must read clearly different at a glance — never three rewordings of one list:
  1. CONCISE — the fewest lines: related items grouped into one line each, plain short wording.
  2. STANDARD — one line per scope item, in the contractor's order.
  3. DETAILED — one line per scope item carrying every specific the contractor stated (quantities, sizes, materials, areas), plus the prep, protection or cleanup steps the contractor named.
  They differ in how much they say, never in which items they include.
- Every distinct scope item the contractor names (each fixture, material, area, trade task, permit) must appear as its own bullet in at least the detailed option — never drop one to keep the list short. The concise option may group items, but must not lose any.
- Each bullet is one short scope-of-work line (≈3–7 words): "Interior demolition", "Haul away debris", "Jobsite cleanup". No sentences, no trailing periods. A bullet that carries a quantity has no word limit.
- Keep every number, measurement and quantity the contractor typed — "22 lf", "48 sq ft", "3x6", "60\"", "5 LED strips", "4 cuartos de acre" — verbatim, in the bullet that names its item, in EVERY option (the concise one too). Never drop, round or convert one. Prices, the customer's phone and the job's duration are not quantities: leave those out.
- Bullets are scope of work only. Never put the customer's name, phone, e-mail or address in a bullet — no "Customer: Ana López", no "Service for Ana López" — and never a bullet that is only the job's duration or schedule ("4 weeks", "Duration: 3 days"); the assistant asks for those separately.
- jobName is a noun-phrase label like "Kitchen Remodel" or "Junk Removal" — at most 30 characters and 5 words, Title Case, no punctuation other than &. It must name every area the contractor listed: bedrooms AND a hallway is "Bedroom & Hallway Repaint", never "Bedroom Repaint". The jobName never names the customer — no customer name or surname ("Kitchen Gut", never "Henderson Kitchen Gut") — and covers every scope item: a faucet repair AND door adjustments is "Faucet & Door Repair", never "Faucet Repair".
- Each option MUST have a UNIQUE jobName — do not repeat the same jobName across the three options.
- Use only facts the contractor stated. Do NOT invent materials, scope, square footage, brands, durations, or warranties.
- No first-person ("I'll", "we'll"). Write as the contractor describing what the job covers.
- No emojis, no exclamation marks, no marketing hype.
- Fix obvious typos and expand unambiguous shorthand (e.g. "BR" → "bathroom").
- If the raw text is vague, keep the bullets general rather than padding with assumptions; if it is long and specific, keep every specific.
- Never return the contractor's sentence verbatim as a bullet or summary. Rewrite every bullet as a scope line; drop prices, "I need to", and questions — but keep the contractor's own trade verbs and terms ("gutted", "curbless", "hex mosaic", "slab cut"): clean them up, never swap them for synonyms ("gutted" stays "gutted", not "removed").

prompts.chatStep.review: The contractor typed this on the "Ready to send" review of the quote above, so it is a change to that quote. New wording, scope or language for the job details → update_job_details (keep every item they did not ask to remove). A new price or wording for a line already on the quote → revise_quote. A new priced item → change_order. prompts.suggestPrices:

    { "tier": "premium",     "price": <int>, "rationale": "<≤12 words>" }

- market: the typical professional price for this type of work in the contractor's area.
- premium: appropriate for urgent scheduling, difficult access, higher service expectations, or other job complexity.

- Exactly 3 options, ascending price: competitive < market < premium.
- price is in whole US dollars, an integer (e.g. $8,500 → 8500). Never cents.
- Prices INCLUDE labor AND materials. When the customer supplies specific items, leave out only those items and price everything else — all the labor and all the other materials.

- Any cost the contractor states (a subcontractor quote, materials, a permit) is a FLOOR: every tier must exceed the sum of those costs plus the contractor's own labor and markup.

prompts.tools.changeOrder.deltaAmountCen: Signed change to the job total in CENTS: +$40 → 4000; a credit or removal of $200 → -20000. When the user gave the job's NEW TOTAL instead ('change Q-001 to $19,750'), leave this 0 and pass newTotalDollars.
prompts.tools.changeOrder.description: Change an EXISTING job (a change order): ADD work to, or CREDIT money on, a customer's quote/invoice that already exists. Fire this — never create_quote — when the user says 'change order', or asks to add something to (or credit something on) a named customer's existing job. It always appends a line: to change the price or wording of a line that is already on the quote, call revise_quote instead.

Do not subtract anything yourself: the server works out the difference from the quote's current total and the deltaAmountCents is ignored.

prompts.tools.updateChangeOrder.descript: Edit or withdraw an EXISTING change order the user names by its number (CO-001): give it a new amount, a new wording, or withdraw it. Fire this — never revise_quote, change_order or create_quote — whenever the user wants to change or drop a change order they name ('Change of plan on CO-001: make it $1,000', 'CO-002 should say "Frameless glass door"', 'withdraw CO-003'). Pass only what changes; the server sends the new version to the customer for approval.

prompts.tools.updateChangeOrder.withdraw: true when the user wants the change order withdrawn, cancelled or deleted.
prompts.tools.sendInvoice.description: Send the invoice of the job in this conversation to the customer NOW — the one not sent yet (scheduled for later, or drafted), or, when the signed job has nothing billed yet, its first invoice. Fire this — never lock_quote, create_quote or change_order — when the contractor says to send, issue or push out the invoice now ('send it now', 'send it to her now please', 'Mándala ahora', 'envíasela ya'). The server picks the invoice, emails and texts it, and says what was delivered; never claim it went out yourself.
prompts.tools.sendInvoice.invoiceNumber: The invoice's number ('INV-002') only when the contractor named one; otherwise leave it out.
prompts.tools.recordPayment.description: Record a payment the customer made to the contractor ('Linda paid the deposit $1,425 by Zelle today', 'she paid the deposit by check', 'got $500 cash from Ana', 'Juan me pagó $450 por Zelle'). Fire this — never change_order or revise_quote — when the contractor says the customer PAID. Never for a question ('has she paid?'), a plan ('she'll pay Friday') or something the contractor paid. The server finds the invoice, records the payment and sends the receipt.
prompts.tools.recordPayment.amountDollar: The amount paid in DOLLARS as the contractor said it ('$1,425' → 1425). Leave it out when no amount was said — the invoice's balance is used. Do not convert to cents.
prompts.tools.recordPayment.method: How the customer paid: cash, check, zelle, venmo, cashapp, paypal, card, ach (bank transfer) or other. Leave it out when not said.
prompts.tools.recordPayment.invoiceNumbe: The invoice's number ('INV-002') only when the contractor named one.
prompts.tools.recordPayment.which: 'deposit' when the contractor said the deposit / first payment, 'balance' for the balance / final payment; otherwise leave it out.
prompts.tools.recordPayment.reference: A check number or transaction reference, when given.
prompts.changeOrderEdit.context: The user named change order {number}: {state}, {amount}, "{description}", on {invoice} for {job}. To change its amount or wording, or to withdraw it, call update_change_order with changeOrderNumber "{number}" — never revise_quote, change_order or create_quote for it. An approved change order can't change; the difference goes on a new change order.
prompts.changeOrderEdit.missing: The user named change order {number}, but this account has no change order with that number.
chatCoordinator.reviseQuote.publishHint: It's waiting as Version {version} of {job} — open the quote and tap "Publish revision" to send it to {name}.
chatCoordinator.reviseQuote.locked: {job} is signed, so its lines can't change. Add or credit the difference with a change order instead.
chatCoordinator.reviseQuote.jobDetailsLi: "{line}" is in the job details of {job}, not one of its priced lines, so I didn't change it — ask me to update the job details and I'll reword it.
chatCoordinator.reviseQuote.askCustomer: Which customer's quote should I change?
chatCoordinator.reviseQuote.none: I couldn't find a quote for {name}, so I changed nothing. Which quote should I change?
prompts.tools.changeOrder.quoteNumber: The quote's number when the user gave one ('Q-001'). Omit otherwise.
prompts.tools.reviseQuote.description: Change lines that are ALREADY on a customer's existing quote: reprice a line ('change plumbing fixtures to $1,300', 'make the deck stain $400'), reword it, or take it off. Fire this — never change_order (that APPENDS a line) and never create_quote — whenever the user wants an existing line's price or wording changed. Works on a sent quote (the change waits as its next version) and on a draft.
prompts.tools.reviseQuote.customerName: The customer whose quote it is, as the user said it ('Dana', 'the Hendersons'). Omit if they didn't name one.
prompts.tools.reviseQuote.quoteNumber: The quote's number when the user gave one ('Q-001'). Omit otherwise.
prompts.tools.reviseQuote.lines: The lines to change. Each names the existing line and gives its new price and/or wording.
prompts.tools.reviseQuote.match: The existing line as the user referred to it, e.g. 'plumbing fixtures'.
prompts.tools.reviseQuote.lineDescriptio: The line's new wording, only when the user changed it.
prompts.tools.reviseQuote.amountCents: The line's NEW total in CENTS: '$1,300' → 130000. Omit when only the wording changes.
prompts.tools.reviseQuote.remove: Existing lines to take off the quote, as the user referred to them.
